name: Vitamin D and K2 for teeth

lead: Some people take vitamins D and K2 hoping to help enamel and dentin remineralise and keep teeth strong-looking. The idea draws on the roles these vitamins play in bone mineralisation.

Vitamin K2 is a cofactor for osteocalcin, a protein involved in bone mineral formation. Clinical data on K2 for bone are described as inconclusive, and no studies of vitamins D and K2 for tooth remineralisation were found.

paras: They are taken as supplements or from foods such as fatty fish, egg yolks and fermented foods, usually as part of a broader nutrition-for-teeth approach alongside brushing and fluoride.
No dental-specific risks are documented. Vitamin K2 may interact with anticoagulants, so anyone on blood thinners would check with a clinician.

chain: Vitamins D and K2 support mineralisation
angle.text: Folk claims hold that vitamins D and K2 help teeth remineralise and rebuild, borrowing from bone research where K2 aids mineral formation. Dental trials of the idea have not been run.

lead: Vitamin D and vitamin K2 are discussed in folk claims that they help teeth remineralise. Vitamin K2 is a cofactor for osteocalcin, a protein involved in bone mineral formation.[1]
Clinical data on K2 for bone are described as inconclusive, and the K2 reference text contains no dental content.[1] No studies of vitamin D and K2 for tooth remineralisation were found.

paras: Vitamin K2 activates vitamin K-dependent proteins such as osteocalcin; in vitro studies show effects on osteoblast differentiation, and bone effects may be stronger with vitamin D.[1] Application of these findings to teeth has not been established.
